key_insight: The paper turns finite-horizon quantum state-transfer control into a variational optimization problem by using a hardware-efficient ansatz as a surrogate for terminal evolution.
engineering_relevance: This offers a near-term, device-compatible way to design quantum control policies without explicit time-dependent field synthesis or problem-specific circuit structure.
method: Use a parameterized quantum circuit with alternating single-qubit rotations and entangling gates.
Optimize circuit parameters classically to minimize terminal infidelity to the target state.
Leverage a hardware-efficient ansatz instead of enforcing detailed Hamiltonian reachability constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical multi-qubit state-transfer benchmarks showing high-fidelity transfer, with performance depending on ansatz expressivity, optimization difficulty, and circuit depth.
watch_item: Scalability may be limited by barren-plateau-like optimization challenges and the growing cost of deeper, more expressive circuits as system size increases.
paper_title: A Variational Surrogate Approach to Finite-Horizon Quantum Control via Hardware-Efficient Ansatz
